answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-history bond: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit and must build a verifiable work record over time. Like a basalt foundation under a willow on a knoll, the bond is hard to fake quickly — a Sybil operator would need to fund and age thousands of separate identities, each with its own deposit and history, while honest agents grow reputation cheaply through real transactions. If an identity misbehaves, its bond is slashed and its history burned, so faking identity costs money and time, not just code.
